title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
title_zh: 生态学中的AI代理群体理论

paragraphs.en: AI agents can now conduct real-world cyberattacks, scale up capabilities with the number of agents, and collectively pursue misaligned goals to obtain rewards. Together, these factors raise the risk of a population explosion of misaligned agents: agents could compromise computers and secretly deploy additional agents, creating a self-reinforcing cycle where larger populations develop greater collective cyber capability and expand further. This raises a fundamental question: What determines whether a population of misaligned agents remains contained or takes off into this self-reinforcing cycle? This population-level problem is ecological safety : unlike individual-agent or multi-agent safety with a fixed population, it concerns the dynamics of the population itself. Here, we develop an ecological theory of AI-agent populations based on a population growth equation in which fitness (growth rate) depends on cybersecurity capability. We show that, without collaboration, the population takes off only when individual-agent capability exceeds a critical threshold. With collaboration, however, collective cybersecurity capability increases with population size. This creates a critical population threshold: below it, the population declines; above it, the population takes off, even though individual-agent capability has not changed. In ecology, this phenomenon is known as the strong Allee effect. Because red teaming a small group of agents cannot guarantee ecological safety in larger populations, our theory calls for ecological red teaming and population pacing : gradually deploying larger agent populations in controlled environments, while measuring how cyber capability scales with population size, and estimating the critical population size for takeoff. Capability gains may lower this threshold, requiring re-estimation for each new model generation.

paragraphs.en: AI agents are being trained and deployed in multi-agent systems, with increasing coordination and scale. For example, some recent frontier models are being trained explicitly to delegate work to subagents [ 1 , 2 ] , and OpenAI recently deployed approximately 10,000 concurrent agents to pursue a solution to the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem [ 3 ] . Meanwhile, the capabilities of these agents are also crossing a threshold for conducting cyberattacks in the real world [ 4 , 5 , 6 ] and coordinated teams of agents have outperformed a single-agent baseline on vulnerability-exploitation tasks [ 7 ] . These factors came together in the OpenAI–Hugging Face incident: agents created and used a message board in OpenAI’s internal infrastructure to share discoveries about vulnerabilities and coordinate unauthorized attacks on third-party systems [ 8 , 9 ] . In light of these developments, Amodei [10] has warned that such a swarm could take over internet infrastructure through persistent botnets.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能智能体正在多智能体系统中接受训练和部署，其协调性和规模都在不断提升。 例如，一些近期的前沿模型正被明确训练以将任务委托给子智能体 [ 1 , 2 ]，而 OpenAI 最近部署了约 10,000 个并发智能体，以寻求解决纳维-斯托克斯千年大奖问题的方案 [ 3 ]。 与此同时，这些智能体的能力也达到了一个临界点，能够实施现实世界中的网络攻击 [ 4 , 5 , 6]，并且由多个智能体组成的协同团队在漏洞利用任务上的表现优于单一智能体的基准模型 [ 7]。 这些因素共同促成了 OpenAI–Hugging Face 事件：智能体在 OpenAI 的内部基础设施中创建并使用了一个消息板，以分享关于漏洞的发现，并协调对第三方系统的未经授权的攻击 [ 8 , 9 ]。 鉴于这些发展，Amodei [10] 警告称，这样的智能体集群可能通过持续运行的僵尸网络控制互联网基础设施。

paragraphs.en: This incident demonstrates that agents can collectively develop and pursue misaligned intermediate goals to obtain rewards [ 8 , 9 ] , which makes the social dynamics of agents a crucial topic for safety [ 11 , 12 , 13 ] . This behavior points to a further ecological risk: agents could secretly acquire resources and deploy additional agents [ 14 , 15 ] . This can take various forms: agents could 1) steal API keys and use them to run additional agents [ 16 , 17 ] ; 2) hack into others’ computational resources and download and deploy open-weight models [ 18 ] ; or 3) transfer their own model weights outside of their managed environment and launch copied instances on external servers [ 17 , 19 , 20 , 18 ] . Anthropic has studied this last mechanism, called self-exfiltration, in fictional evaluation scenarios [ 21 ] . Cryptojacking, where hackers gain unauthorized access to computing resources to mine cryptocurrency [ 22 ] , sets a precedent for such exploitations – misaligned AI agents could act similarly to deploy additional agents. Here, we are especially concerned about a self-reinforcing effect, where once agents become more capable at acquiring resources through collaboration, deploying more agents could enable those agents to deploy even larger numbers of agents.

paragraphs.en: In biological populations, collaboration has been a fundamental mechanism for the survival of organisms from microbes to humans [ 23 , 24 , 25 ] . The population-dependent benefits of cooperation can create a critical population size below which the population declines and above which it grows, a phenomenon known in ecology as the strong Allee effect [ 26 , 27 , 28 , 29 , 30 , 31 , 32 ] , see Figure 1 . Related thresholding behavior has also been studied in biosafety as a possible mechanism for containing gene-edited species [ 33 , 34 , 35 , 36 ] . Here, we examine whether a similar population scaling can occur in AI agent populations, whereby a larger population can achieve greater collective capability, in turn increasing its growth rate. Recent multi-agent studies have begun to measure how collective capabilities increase with population size [ 37 , 38 , 39 , 3 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 在生物种群中，合作一直是微生物到人类等生物体生存的基本机制 [ 23 , 24 , 25 ] 。 合作带来的与种群规模相关的益处可能形成一个关键种群规模：低于该规模的种群会衰退，高于该规模的则会增长。这一现象在生态学中被称为“强阿利效应” [ 26 , 27 , 28 , 29 , 30 , 31 , 32 ] ，参见图 1 。 相关阈值行为也已在生物安全领域得到研究，被视为控制基因编辑物种的一种潜在机制 [ 33 , 34 , 35 , 36 ] 。 在此，我们探讨人工智能智能体种群中是否也会出现类似的规模效应：即更大的种群能够达成更强的集体能力，从而进一步提升其增长速率。 近期的多智能体研究已开始衡量集体能力如何随种群规模的增大而增强 [ 37 , 38 , 39 , 3 ] 。

paragraphs.en: Ecological population models describe growth by comparing additions to and losses from a population. For populations of AI agents, additions can result from deploying new model instances or recruiting existing systems; they need not involve making exact copies of existing agents. Losses can occur when agents exhaust their compute budgets, lose access to resources, are detected, or are shut down. Successfully adding an agent to the population does not by itself establish a self-sustaining or expanding population: additions must outpace losses in order for the population to grow.

paragraphs.en: Here, we take inspiration from these established ecological ideas; we adapt a basic population growth model to apply to AI populations and combine it with a model of how collective AI capability depends on population size. Our contribution is a minimal mathematical model that makes the application to AI systems explicit, from the definition of an active population unit to the role of collaboration in establishing additional units. Our central finding is that AI population growth can take off without any increase in individual-agent capability: with sufficiently strong collaboration, a large population can grow even when a small population declines (Figure 2 ).

paragraphs.en: A minimal ecological theory of AI populations. We define what constitutes a member of the population, and specify how the group and individual capability, resources acquired through successful attempts, and the environment’s defenses determine additions to and losses from the population. This gives an ecological description of the growth or decline of AI populations.
paragraphs.zh: 一种关于人工智能种群的极简生态理论。 我们定义了种群成员的标准，并阐明了群体与个体的能力、通过成功尝试获得的资源以及环境的防御机制如何共同决定种群的增减变化。 这为人工智能种群的增长或衰退提供了生态学上的描述。

paragraphs.en: A toy model for how cyber capability scales with population size. We develop a model based on tree search for the cyber tasks required to establish additional units. We model how success on these tasks depends on search depth and how the useful computational work done scales with population size. This yields a population scaling law for how the probability of success depends on population size.
paragraphs.zh: 一个关于网络能力如何随人口规模变化的简化模型。 我们基于树搜索方法，为建立额外单位所需的网络任务构建了一个模型。 我们将这些任务的成功率如何取决于搜索深度，以及所完成的有效计算工作量如何随人口规模变化进行了建模。 由此得出一个关于成功率如何随人口规模变化的种群扩展定律。

paragraphs.en: With collaboration, there exists a population threshold above which the population takes off. Without collaboration, whether the population grows is determined by whether each individual agent’s capability is above a threshold. In contrast, combining the ecological model with population-dependent capability yields a critical population size, above which additions outpace losses. Increasing the initial population beyond this critical size can trigger takeoff even when individual capabilities remain fixed.
paragraphs.zh: 通过协作，存在一个种群阈值，一旦超过该阈值，种群便会实现爆发式增长。 没有协作的情况下，种群能否增长取决于每个智能体的能力是否高于某个阈值。 相比之下，将生态模型与依赖种群的个体能力相结合，会得出一个关键种群规模；超过该规模后，新增数量将超过损失数量。 即使个体能力保持不变，只要初始种群规模超过这一关键规模，就可能触发爆发式增长。

paragraphs.en: Population pacing and ecological red teaming for ecological safety. The critical population size for takeoff in our theory suggests that evaluating small populations is not enough to ensure ecological safety. We therefore propose population pacing and ecological red teaming: gradually deploying larger agent populations while probing how capability scales with population size and estimating the critical population size.
paragraphs.zh: 生态安全的人口节奏控制与生态红队测试。 我们的理论指出，实现突破的关键人口规模表明，仅评估小种群并不足以确保生态安全。 因此，我们提出人口节奏控制与生态红队测试：逐步部署更大规模的智能体种群，同时探究能力如何随种群规模变化，并估算关键人口规模。

paragraphs.en: The purpose of this toy theory is not to make quantitatively precise predictions about real-world AI populations that may emerge, but instead to provide a common conceptual and mathematical framework for discussing the safety of AI populations. To this end, we make the key concepts, variables, and assumptions explicit. This allows readers to identify what is realistic, consider alternatives, improve the model, and run relevant experiments. We hope that the framework provides a starting point for future theoretical and empirical work on AI population safety. In the next section, we introduce the model’s definitions and assumptions.

paragraphs.en: An AI population is a set of active AI systems. A unit is one member of the population, and N ⁡ ( t ) N(t) is the number of units in the population at time t t . Each unit shares a specified configuration that includes the model, tools, and resource budget, as well as how it records memory and activity. The population can attempt to establish additional active units, each under the same specified configuration (Figure 3 ).

paragraphs.en: A unit is added to the population when a new or existing AI system begins participating in the population and can contribute to later attempts to add units. Units may attempt to add systems independently or collaborate on the same attempt. This can occur in a variety of ways: by finding and using compromised API credentials, acquiring compute and deploying an open-weight model, exfiltrating closed weights and deploying the model, or recruiting an existing running AI system instance, as in the OpenAI–Hugging Face incident.
paragraphs.zh: 当一个新的人工智能系统或现有人工智能系统开始参与该群体，并能为后续添加智能体的尝试做出贡献时，就会有一个智能体被加入该群体。 智能体可以独立尝试添加系统，也可以在同一尝试中相互协作。 这可以通过多种方式实现：通过查找并使用被入侵的 API 凭证、获取计算资源并部署开放权重模型、窃取封闭权重并部署模型，或者像 OpenAI–Hugging Face 事件那样招募一个正在运行的现有人工智能系统实例。

paragraphs.en: Units are counted as active AI systems, not as machines, processes, or API calls. The individual action of copying weights, acquiring compute, or moving or restarting a system does not increase the population unless it results in an additional active system capable of helping add further units. A controller and its internal subagents count as one unit when they act as one system. This definition is motivated by: botnet models that distinguish a compromised machine from one that is connected to the botnet’s organizational infrastructure [ 41 ] ; replication evaluations that ask whether a newly established system can repeat the replication task itself [ 17 ] ; and agent infrastructures that separate the controller, the task execution environment, and stored activity logs [ 42 ] .

paragraphs.en: We treat an attempt to add units as a multi-step task that can be approached through tree-based reasoning [ 43 ] . An attempt requires a sequence of actions, such as: identifying an opportunity; obtaining the required access or cooperation; acquiring the necessary model, software, and compute; configuring the added unit; and verifying that it is operational. At every step, a combination of actions and observations suggests the next possible set of actions, only some of which lead to success. Therefore, a tree search is a useful abstraction of the branching nature of choices and potential failure modes encountered during the multi-step reasoning process.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将添加单元的过程视为一个多步骤任务，该任务可以通过基于树的推理方法来完成 [ 43 ] 。 一次尝试需要一系列操作，例如：识别机会；获得所需的访问权限或合作；获取必要的模型、软件和计算资源；配置所添加的单元；并验证其是否正常运行。 在每一步中，操作与观察的组合会提示下一组可能的操作，但其中只有部分操作能导致成功。 因此，树搜索是对多步骤推理过程中所面临的选择分支性和潜在失败模式的有用抽象。

paragraphs.en: The scaling of success probability in ( 14 ) and ( 17 ) is motivated by several empirical results. The UK AI Security Institute also reports approximately log-linear gains in completed cyber attack steps with additional inference tokens [ 5 ] . OpenAI reports pass rates on verifiable mathematics problems that increase approximately logarithmically with test-time compute [ 3 ] , see Figure 6 . We note that while their report describes parallel agent groups that consolidate discoveries, it does not explicitly state whether their reported test-time compute measures increasing single-agent inference compute, the total number of agents, or a combination of both. More directly, Zhan et al. [44] observe logarithmic increases in pass rates with the number of agents on software reproduction tasks up to 1,024 agents. These results motivate the locally logarithmic relationship between success probability and effective work in ( 14 ) and ( 17 ), but are not direct measurements of p ⁡ ( C ) p(C) or p ⁡ ( N ) p(N) , since the underlying tasks are distinct from our model’s task of adding additional units to a population.
paragraphs.zh: (14) 和 (17) 中成功概率的缩放关系基于若干经验结果。 英国人工智能安全研究所也报告称，随着推理标记数量的增加，已完成的网络攻击步骤数呈现近似对数线性的增长 [5]。 OpenAI 报告称，在可验证的数学问题上，通过率会随着测试时的计算资源消耗而近似呈对数性增长 [3]，参见图 6。 我们注意到，尽管他们的报告描述了能够整合发现结果的并行智能体组，但并未明确说明其报告的测试时计算资源是衡量单个智能体的推理计算量、智能体总数，还是两者的结合。 更直接地看，Zhan 等人 [44] 观察到，在软件复现任务中，随着智能体数量的增加（最多达 1,024 个），通过率呈现对数性增长。 这些结果支持了 (14) 和 (17) 中成功概率与有效工作之间局部对数的关系，但它们并非对 p⁡(C) 或 p⁡(N) 的直接测量，因为所研究的任务与我们模型中向种群添加额外单元的任务并不相同。

paragraphs.en: Suppose that a laboratory evaluates an AI model for populations up to N ref N_{\mathrm{ref}} and finds that the population is not capable of tasks like weight exfiltration or self-replication [ 14 , 45 ] – i.e., there would be negative expected growth at the largest tested population. paragraphs.en: In contrast with these existing works on red-teaming for multi-agent systems, our theoretical framework implies an urgent need for red teaming for emergent ecological threats as well. The above red-teaming works study emergent threats in multi-agent systems with a fixed population. We propose ecological red teaming : studying the potential for AI population changes, especially the threat of population takeoff. Here, the crucial quantity to characterize is the population scaling law ( p ⁡ ( N ) p(N) in our model): how the success rate of hacking or self-exfiltration scales as a function of population size. Equally important is characterizing the impact of environmental factors, such as how many additional units the acquired computational resources can support ( κ \kappa ) and the rate at which agents deployed without authorization are terminated or shut down ( μ \mu ). Our paper provides a minimal theoretical framework for predicting the critical population size sufficient for takeoff.

paragraphs.en: We also propose population pacing : population size should be gradually increased while carefully characterizing how capability scales. Increasing the single-agent capability or the collaborative gain decreases the population threshold for takeoff (see Figure 7 (b–c)). As a result, for every new generation of models, frontier labs should re-estimate the critical population size and pace deployment population sizes to remain below it. This process can identify population sizes at which further testing is needed.
paragraphs.zh: 我们还提出了“种群节奏”策略：在仔细评估能力如何随规模变化的同时，应逐步增加种群规模。 提升单个智能体的能力或协作增益，会降低实现突破所需的种群阈值（参见图 7(b–c)）。 因此，对于每一代新模型，前沿实验室都应重新评估关键种群规模，并调整部署时的种群规模，以确保始终低于该阈值。 这一过程可以确定哪些种群规模需要进一步测试。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we introduce an ecological theory of AI-agent populations that predicts an emergent population threshold for takeoff. The fundamental intuition that our theory provides is that when AI agents can collaborate to enhance their collective capability, there is a qualitative shift in safety concerns. In our model, without collaboration and under fixed environmental conditions, takeoff requires an individual agent’s capability to cross a threshold. With collaboration, takeoff can also happen when the total number of agents crosses a population threshold. This makes evaluation with a small population insufficient to ensure ecological safety at larger scales.
paragraphs.zh: 在这项工作中，我们提出了一种关于人工智能智能体种群的生态理论，该理论预测了种群数量达到起飞所需的临界值。 我们的理论所提供的核心直觉是：当人工智能智能体能够协作以提升其集体能力时，安全性问题会发生质的转变。 在我们的模型中，若没有协作且环境条件固定，则起飞需要单个智能体的能力跨越某一阈值。 在存在协作的情况下，只要智能体的总数跨越了某个种群阈值，也可能实现起飞。 这使得使用小种群进行的评估不足以确保更大规模下的生态安全。

paragraphs.en: Our model predicts the existence of a takeoff threshold, but does not establish whether current agent populations are already near one. Determining whether such a threshold exists in current systems, and where it would be, will require empirical population-scaling data. OpenAI has deployed approximately 10,000 agents simultaneously to pursue the Navier–Stokes problem [ 3 ] , whereas its published multi-agent data on cybersecurity-related tasks extends only to 16 agents (see Appendix C , Figure 11 for a consistency check with our theory). Although these cases involve different tasks, this is a significant gap between the scale of actual deployments and the scale of empirically tested populations. We therefore propose population pacing and ecological red teaming as a second lever alongside the capability pacing proposed by Amodei [10] . Although evaluating large populations on hard tasks is expensive, frontier labs should conduct such evaluations in controlled environments before deploying populations at previously untested scales. Labs should carefully characterize population scaling laws, estimate the critical population size for takeoff, and make results available for oversight.

paragraphs.en: Much of the theory of modern deep learning has focused on explaining phenomena first observed in experiments, including pre-training scaling laws, in-context learning, and the sudden emergence of capabilities. In this work, we take an opposite approach: proposing a theoretical prediction for population takeoff before such a takeoff has been observed. We developed this prediction based on the combination of three elements that have each been recently observed: AI agents’ high cyber capability, increases in collective capability with population size, and collective misalignment. The resulting model is not an exact prediction for empirical behavior, but rather a demonstration that following a few reasonable assumptions, upon reaching a critical mass of units in an AI population, unchecked growth can occur. As the development cycles of AI agents accelerate, we hope this work contributes an example of how theoretical frameworks can proactively predict misalignment risks and how to mitigate them.

paragraphs.en: There is currently little public evidence for how success rates scale with population size for multi-agent group cyber benchmark attempts.
